svg.aria-label: Sequence diagram of a put over a key whose earlier put is being copied to cold: Client, Node, Leader, Hot tier, Cold tier. The leader holds the entry for the copy. The node amends the entry into its own replace put, replaces the hot object, and acknowledges. The leader finishes streaming the old object into cold, its seal fails because the entry changed, and the next pass copies the new object over the old one with If-Match on the cold tag.
svg.title: An overwrite while the leader copies the previous put: the entry is amended, the copy is superseded
svg.text: An overwrite while the leader copies the previous put: the entry is amended, the copy is superseded
Client
Node
Leader
Hot tier
Cold tier
start: hot holds v1, entry (PUT, PENDING), cold has no object; the put of v1
was acknowledged
A1 CAS (PUT,PENDING) to (PUT,HELD,leader)
A2 stream v1 from hot, create-only publish at the end
B0 PUT key (v2)
B1 create entry: EXISTS; read it: (PUT,HELD,leader)
B2 CAS (PUT,HELD,leader) to (PUT,HELD,node,replace)
amend: the leader keeps copying, this put does not wait for it
B3 hot HEAD key (v1), cold HEAD key (absent)
B4 replace key in hot, If-Match on the tag of v1: now v2
B5 CAS entry to (PUT,PENDING,replace)
B6 200: v2 is acknowledged; every read finds
v2 in hot
A3 the publish of v1 lands: cold holds v1 (hidden by hot)
A4 CAS to SEALED fails: the entry is not the one it held
it releases nothing and goes on to the next pass
C1 next pass: CAS (PUT,PENDING,replace) to (PUT,HELD,leader,replace)
C2 cold HEAD (v1 tag), stream v2 from hot, replace If-Match on the v1 tag
C3 CAS to SEALED, delete the entry: cold and hot both hold v2
A copy that was started before the overwrite can publish after it. That is safe because hot holds v2 for the whole time and a read finds hot
first; nothing evicts a key that has an entry. A cold publish of v1 by a stalled leader after C2 is a create-only write against an existing object
and fails. A delete that meets the leader's copy waits for the release (the delete diagram); an overwrite does not, because it leaves an object in
hot and a delete does not. An overwrite that lands in the cold tier (a multipart completion) does wait (section 5.3).
